subject: Tenant shadow networking & egress attestation
messages:
From: Luis Mendoza <luis.mendoza@shadowgrid.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: ShadowGrid Security <security@shadowgrid.com>, ops-contacts@shadowgrid.com
Date: 2027-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant shadow networking & initial egress attestation request

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the intro call last week. We're progressing on our end to onboard a ShadowGrid tenant into Redwood Private (VPC). Before we schedule the architecture review, Security has asked for a short attestation around the proposed "shadow" networking pattern — specifically how control plane traffic is isolated from tenant data plane egress and what mechanisms are in place to prevent accidental exfiltration to public endpoints.

Attached: shadowgrid-attachment-egress-policy.pdf (PDF) and a quick sketch (design-v1.png). High-level asks:
- Confirm control plane endpoints that will be contacted from the tenant private fabric (FQDNs and IP ranges if possible).
- Describe egress policy options you support: NAT, egress proxy with allowlist, private endpoints (VPC endpoints), or force-tunnel to customer-managed inspection.
- KV/cache behavior: will any model shards or caches contact external CDNs or telemetry endpoints? If so, can that be routed via customer egress?
- Evidence: a short runbook or checklist we can present to our auditors (SOC2) describing the acceptance criteria.

Target timeline: we'd like a readout and preliminary answers by EOD Friday (10/08) so we can line up our compliance review. If there are show-stoppers that need infra changes on your side, flag them.

Would appreciate if you loop in your networking/security SMEs — cc'ing security so they see the ask.

Thanks,
Luis Mendoza
Director, Infrastructure — ShadowGrid
-----
ShadowGrid Inc.
luis.mendoza@shadowgrid.com | +1 415 555 0189
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant shadow networking & initial egress attestation request

Luis — thanks for the clear list. Kim and Jasmine are copied; they'll take point on the low-level network proofing and the attestation checklist respectively. Quick replies inline below, and we've attached a preliminary wireframe we call "redwood-vpc-wireframe-v1.svg" that shows control vs data plane surfaces for a typical tenant private deployment.

Short answers (preliminary):
- Control plane endpoints: our control plane uses regional endpoints that terminate mTLS with customer-managed CA when Private mode is enabled. We can provide FQDNs and CIDR blocks for the regional control plane (us-west-2) — will send ranges in a follow-up once we confirm the locked list with infra.
- Egress options supported: NAT through customer-managed gateway (recommended for visibility), egress proxy (we can point to an allowlist), or forced private endpoints for some services. We do NOT call any public CDNs for KV cache traffic by default; telemetry can be configured to route to customer endpoints or disabled.
- KV/Cache: our runtime keeps KV cache local to the tenant fabric; background model artifact fetches are only during image/asset pulls and can be pinned to a mirror you manage.
- Evidence/runbook: Jasmine will draft a short attestation template + checklist based on your SOC2 needs.

Action items we own before Friday:
1) Confirm FQDNs/CIDRs for control plane endpoints (Rafael)
2) Draft attestation/runbook v0 (Jasmine)
3) Wireframe + recommended egress pattern (Kim)

Can we do a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the wireframe live? Proposed slots: 10:00–10:30 PT or 15:00–15:30 PT.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 206 555 0192
Redwood Inference — Private Deployments

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant shadow networking & initial egress attestation request

Hi team — following up with concrete patterns and a short redline of the wireframe. Inline notes follow the SVG sections (copied for ease):

- Control plane (management traffic):
  * mTLS-only endpoints, allowlist at IP + FQDN level. We recommend an explicit control-plane CIDR block in the customer's FW for ingest (we'll provide it).
  * Health-checks and telemetry toward our control plane are optional; if ShadowGrid disables remote telemetry, we run in observation-lite mode and surface metrics via the console only when you pull them over the management channel.

- Tenant data plane (in-subnet):
  * Primary egress recommendation: route tenant data-plane outbound through customer-managed NAT/inspection (recommended for SOC2 evidence).
  * Alternative: egress proxy that performs allowlist/denylist for runtime calls (we can operate with either).
  * Do NOT enable any optional background artifact update jobs to public endpoints unless ShadowGrid provides a mirrored repository.

Operational items (short):
1) Please provide the account IDs and VPC CIDRs we should expect for the tenant testbed.
2) If you want us to stand up an egress-proxy example, we can push a containerized demo into your staging tenant and provide iptables/nginx config snippets. (Jira: JIRA-OPS-4127)
3) We prefer canary validation: 50 tenants in a shadow group with forced egress, then expand.

Links and evidence:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_shadowgrid-integration (wireframe + compliance checklist draft)
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-4127 (egress-proxy demo)

I'll attach a short checklist PDF in the next email (attestation checklist v0).

Kimberly Park
